title: Japan’s modeled household consumption falls in real terms while category and household-type exposure diverge
source_unit: Statistics Bureau of Japan Consumer Trend Index (CTI), July 2026, 2025-base revision
geography: Japan; all households, single-person households, two-or-more-person households, and ten major expenditure categories

observations.period: July 2026 compared with July 2025; household consumption trend index

denominator.unit: Japanese household consumption index; CTI combines Family Income and Expenditure Survey, Family Income and Expenditure Survey for One-person Households, and related household-consumption survey inputs

all_households_nominal_yoy.unit: percent year-over-year change in nominal household consumption trend index

all_households_real_yoy.unit: percent year-over-year change in real household consumption trend index

nominal_real_gap.unit: percentage-point difference between nominal and real year-over-year changes

seasonally_adjusted_real_mom.unit: percent month-over-month change in seasonally adjusted real household consumption trend index

mechanism.value: Near-flat nominal consumption can conceal a real contraction when prices absorb household spending; the signal is about purchasing-power-adjusted consumption movement, not only cash outlays

observations.method: Statistics Bureau of Japan CTI July 2026 result overview, 2025=100 base. The household CTI estimates average household consumption by combining Family Income and Expenditure Survey results with household-consumption and single-person-monitor inputs; real values are the published inflation-adjusted index series.
observations.uncertainty: CTI is an estimated index rather than a household panel or direct expenditure total. The Statistics Bureau revises historical values, uses seasonal adjustment, and changed to a 2025 base; nominal-real differences do not identify household-specific inflation, quantities, debt, income, or welfare.
observations.subgroup: Japanese households, including single-person households in the combined total.
observations.counterinterpretation: A real index decline may reflect price deflation treatment, composition, timing, or model revision; it does not mean every household reduced every category or experienced financial hardship.

observations.period: July 2026 compared with July 2025; real consumption by category and household type

denominator.unit: Japanese household consumption trend index category and household-type frames; published index estimates, not disclosed respondent counts

real_category_changes.value: food -2.6%; housing -2.6%; utilities -8.7%; furniture/household goods -5.2%; clothing +2.4%; health/medical -2.0%; transport/communications -1.4%; education -11.8%; culture/recreation -0.7%
real_category_changes.unit: percent year-over-year change in real CTI category indices

single_person_real_yoy.unit: percent year-over-year change in real CTI for single-person households

multi_person_real_yoy.unit: percent year-over-year change in real CTI for two-or-more-person households

household_type_gap.unit: percentage-point difference: multi-person minus single-person real year-over-year decline

category_mechanism.value: Consumption contraction is composition-specific rather than uniform: education and utilities fall much more than culture/recreation, while clothing rises, creating different lived trade-offs across household types and spending baskets

observations.method: Descriptive extraction from the CTI July 2026 result overview, Table 2 and Table 4; category and household-type real year-over-year changes are the published 2025-base index changes.
observations.uncertainty: Category indices are not household budget shares or direct quantities and cannot identify substitution, necessity, price elasticity, access, or cultural meaning. Single-person and multi-person comparisons remain aggregate index differences and inherit CTI revisions and seasonal/model boundaries.
observations.subgroup: Japanese households by household type and ten major consumption categories, including education, utilities, and culture/recreation.
observations.counterinterpretation: A category-level index movement can combine prices, volumes, product quality, timing, and household composition; the 0.6-point household-type gap does not establish unequal hardship or a causal demographic effect.

boundary: This record adds a Japanese modeled consumption, price-pressure, category, and household-type layer. It does not establish household-specific spending, quantities, affordability, debt, income, cultural preference, or causal welfare effects; July 2026 values are revision-sensitive.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Statistics Bureau of Japan CTI landing page, CTI results/methodology page, and July 2026 official result PDF reviewed; all-household nominal and real movements, category changes, household-type comparisons, 2025-base definition, seasonal adjustment, and revision notices checked.
